Marissa — reviewed the redline PDF and summarized my suggested approach below. High-level: we can accept the 24-month term with adjusted renewal notice; we should push back on the indemnity expansion and accept a narrow PHI/data carveout; and we should propose explicit language for proration tied to token start date.

Proposed language snippets (will produce redline PDF):
- Term: "The Initial Term shall be twenty-four (24) months. Thereafter this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party provides not less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice of non-renewal."
- Indemnity: "Each party shall indemnify the other solely for claims arising out of its own gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach; healthcare-data-related claims shall follow the special PHI indemnity in Exhibit C."
- Data residency: "Customer backups are stored in U.S. regions by default. Customer may request EU residency subject to Redwood's capacity and separate agreement for infrastructure costs."
- Proration: "If Customer's Order Form increases capacity mid-invoice period, Customer will be billed a pro rata amount for the remainder of the billing period, calculated on a per-token basis as described in the Billing-Proration-Schedule attached to the Order Form."

Two asks for Marissa/Markus: 1) confirm that the +500k uplift is a recurring monthly commitment that begins on the Effective Date shown on the Order Form; 2) confirm whether we agree to the customer's proposed Exhibit A pricing tiers or whether we should provide a revised tier set (I recommend we keep their numbers but add a transient burst buffer clause).

I'll generate a redline PDF with those edits and share within 2 hours.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-30T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: term change + capacity uplift (MSA redlines)

Marissa / Karthik — finance looked at the OrderForm_Uplift_+500k_2029.xlsx and the Billing-Proration-Schedule. Quick note: first-month proration as requested will reduce the initial invoice by ~34% versus a full month bill if the uplift starts on day 10 of the billing cycle. We can accept the proration language but I recommend we: 1) cap retroactive credits to 30 days, and 2) add language that any SEAT/feature add-ons that change price mid-cycle will be billed at list for the full new month unless pro-rated by written agreement.

Also, for the +500k commitment: confirm whether it's firm committed capacity or a minimum monthly spend tier — that affects revenue recognition. Marissa, do we have a field-sales note on whether they expect to burst past 500k? If yes, we should include a transient burst allowance (e.g., +20% free bursts per month) to avoid immediate overage disputes.

-Markus
Head of Revenue Operations

Jordan / Sandra — thanks for your patience. Please find our consolidated response below and attached redline PDF (Redwood_MSAv3_counter_redline.pdf). Summary of what we can accept and proposed edits: 

- Term: Agreed to 24-month initial term; we propose auto-renew for 12mo with 60-day opt-out (language included in attached redline).
- Capacity uplift: We accept the +500k tokens/month recurring commitment beginning on the Order Form Effective Date. We clarified in the Order Form that "Effective Date" is the date both parties sign the Order Form.
- Proration: We accept a pro rata invoicing approach for mid-cycle uplifts; we added a 30-day cap on retroactive credits and a per-token calculation method in the Billing-Proration-Schedule.
- Indemnity & data residency: We narrowed indemnity to gross negligence/willful misconduct and accepted a PHI carveout per Exhibit C. Backups are hosted in US regions by default; EU residency available via separate infrastructure addendum (language included).

Next steps: 1) Jordan / David — please review the attached counter-redline and the revised Order Form (OrderForm_Rev1.xlsx) and confirm if those changes are acceptable or propose final edits. 2) If we have agreement, we'll prepare DocuSign envelopes for the MSA and Order Form and route for signatures. 3) Finance will produce the first combined invoice reflecting proration examples once Effective Date is agreed.

Target close: EOD Friday. Let me know if you want a 30-minute call to iron final items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
